- **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot V)$, where $N$ is the number of triangles and $V$ is the number of voxels in the triangle's bounding box.
The case-based optimization reduces $V$ for thin triangles.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(M)$, where $M$ is the number of voxels in the partition (`morton_end - morton_start`).
Precision issues may arise with floating-point to integer conversions for grid coordinates.
- **When to Use:** Suitable for building Sparse Voxel Octrees (SVOs) or DAGs from triangle meshes, especially when memory is constrained or the scene has many thin features.
- **When Not to Use:** Not ideal for real-time rendering where precomputed dense grids are preferred, or for scenes with extremely large, thick triangles covering most of the grid.
It is designed for building large-scale sparse voxel structures from triangle meshes, leveraging Morton ordering for efficient spatial indexing and out-of-core processing capabilities.
